S76.03.needs: a signed-in account; a PNG or JPEG image file
S76.03.note: The Vision filter only narrows the list. I found no code in the extension that refuses or reroutes an image turn to a model without vision.
steps: Click the model selector button that shows the current model name.
In the menu labelled Available models, open the drop-down labelled All capabilities and choose Vision.
Check that the list now shows only models with the Vision capability.
Click Add attachment > Upload from device and choose a PNG or JPEG image, then send a message about it.
Compare with Expected: the picker shows image support, and an image turn should not go to a model that cannot read images.
S76.03.where: Model selector button (shows the current model name) > Available models > All capabilities > Vision

S76.04.needs: a signed-in account with file uploads on; two or more image files; a model with a per-message image limit
S76.04.note: The image count comes from model and harness metadata, which I did not read; the exact number shown depends on the chosen model.
steps: Choose a model in the model selector (Available models).
Click Add attachment, then Upload from device, and pick two or more image files.
Click Send.
If the chosen model accepts fewer images, look for the notice that says it accepts up to a number of images and to remove some to send. The message should not send until the count is lowered.
Compare with Expected: the request is checked against the model's image count.
S76.04.where: Add attachment > Upload from device (then Send) with a model that has an image limit

S76.06.needs: a signed-in account with file uploads on; a PDF file
S76.06.note: The composer accepts PDFs; whether a PDF goes natively to a model is not visible in the UI.
steps: Click Add attachment, then Upload from device.
Pick a PDF file and check it is listed in the attachment preview.
Click Send and ask a question that needs the PDF's content.
Compare with Expected: the reply should use the PDF content. The native route versus text extraction is not shown on screen.
S76.06.where: Add attachment > Upload from device (then Send)

S76.26.needs: a signed-in account; a model with effort levels; a Free or lower-plan account to see locked levels
S76.26.note: The Effort section shows only for a model with effort levels; Auto shows effort only after routing.
steps: Click the model selector button and choose a model that has reasoning effort (its menu shows an Effort heading).
Under the Effort heading, look at the rows. Each row name comes from the effort label list (Direct, Brief, Quick, Balanced, Deep, Extended, Maximum); only the levels the model supports appear.
Click a different level and check the row shows as selected and the model badge shows that level.
If a higher level is locked, check its row says Available on [plan] and higher plans.
Compare with Expected: only the model's supported levels are offered and sent.
S76.26.where: Model selector button (shows the current model name) > Effort
